doc: The commute layer (world v87) — machine-readable mirror of world/commute.md. How every working cast member gets from a registered home to a jobs.json employer: mode, legs, leave/arrive windows, weather deltas, shared-route overlaps. Conditions, never scripts — a route is a window the routine layer may satisfy, late or early, and a missed bus is texture, not a bug. INTERNAL tier: spectators read the street texture, never the per-person table.

modes.walk: on foot — the neighborhood default; legs are sidewalk-level
modes.bike: own bike or the courier's frame — fastest door to door, worst in rain
modes.muni: a real Muni line (14, 22, 33, 48, 49, J) — public fact, ride time approximate
modes.muni_walk: bus plus a walk on one or both ends
modes.loop: no single workplace — a circulating route (courier, dog loops, pitches)
modes.stairs: lives above the job — the commute is a staircase

feed_contract: routes never surface to the feed as named people — a route is private logistics. Feed-legible texture is anonymous ('the early wave', 'a rider in the rain'); overlaps are conditions the AI may render, never events the feed announces.
rules: Conditions, never scripts — a route is a window the routine system may satisfy; it can run late, early, or be missed, and a missed 49 is texture, not a broken script.
Minors are never routed — no rows for A04/A20 exist by construction; the school wave is unnamed extras texture (crowd layer), never a per-person route.
Ambient homes stay off-registry — 'ambient-ring' is a direction, not an address; promotion mints a real address per address spec §6 and adds a homes row here.
Weather deltas are modal suggestions — the thin tier may take the suggestion or not; a wet cyclist is a choice, not a violation.
Surface knowledge only — a route says where someone goes, never why they're late, who they met, or what they're avoiding. Secrets live in bibles; the commute layer is a leak-free channel.
No prices anywhere — fares, wages, and costs live in other layers; this file moves bodies, not money.
Every 'to' resolves to a jobs.json employer; every registered 'from' resolves to a housing unit id. New employers or units must land there first.
